views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the already-announced $50B retaliatory list as leverage but do not implement it, and do not add a new tariff tranche, while the U.S. comment/hearing process runs through May. Open talks on market-access items China was already preparing (auto tariffs, licensing, IP enforcement) and press the WTO track, without conceding Made in China 2025 or forced-tech-transfer structure. Treat Trump’s $100B instruction as a live risk: further Chinese escalation now would likely be answered with a broader U.S. list before any duties have even taken effect.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not yet high-anchor. On 22 March the U.S. directed Section 301 tariffs, a WTO case, and investment restrictions; on 3 April USTR published a proposed 25% list of ~1,300 lines (~$50B) aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery — explicitly the Made in China 2025 upgrade path, not just a residual surplus. After China’s 4 April mirror list, Trump instructed USTR to consider another $100B, so the upside risk is a jump from ~10% of China’s U.S. goods exports toward a much larger share. That is why the reading sits above zero. It stays well below +0.5 because nothing on the $50B lists is in force (USTR comment through 11 May, hearing 15 May; Lighthizer said no duties until process completes), China’s real economy is not yet showing a trade-war bite (industrial production ~6–7% y/y, CPI soft, reserves ~$3.14T, yuan stronger at 6.27 vs ~6.59 last autumn, merchandise exports still rising), and China retains political leverage on U.S. soy, autos and aircraft — over a third of U.S. goods exports to China. Action should therefore be talk, not a new strike. China already answered 232 with $3B (2 April) and matched 301 dollar-for-dollar on 4 April; another tariff move now would validate the $100B threat and impose self-harm on soybean supply. Xi’s 10–11 April Boao opening (auto tariff cuts, wider market access, IP) produced a conciliatory Trump response and a market relief bid, creating a window that Chinese officials should use without rolling back the $50B list or buying a purchase package the U.S. has not yet offered.
key_factors: USTR $50B Section 301 list targets MIC 2025 sectors (aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery), not just surplus goods
Trump instruction to consider an additional $100B after China's 4 April mirror list raises escalation risk
Neither $50B list is in force; U.S. comment/hearing window runs into mid-May
China already matched proportionately ($3B on 232; $50B proposed on 301) so further tariff hikes are optional, not required for credibility
Chinese macro still resilient: IP growth, stable reserves, stronger CNY; dispute not yet biting the real economy
Xi Boao opening and Trump's thankful response create a narrow talks window without structural concession
Soy/auto/aircraft targeting gives China farm-belt and industrial leverage but also self-supply risk if implemented

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR releases Section 301 report; Trump memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.

In light of China's unfair retaliation, Trump instructed USTR to consider whether $100 billion of additional tariffs would be appropriate under Section 301. Lighthizer stressed no tariffs take effect until the process is complete.

Proposed list targets products that benefit from China's industrial plans such as Made in China 2025; sectors include aerospace, ICT, robotics, and machinery; public comment and a hearing precede any final list.

$50B is ~10% of China's goods exports to the U.S. but over one-third of U.S. goods exports to China; U.S. soy is over a third of China's soybean imports; neither set of tariffs takes effect immediately.

Xi at Boao pledged wider market access, auto tariff cuts and IP enforcement; Trump tweeted he was thankful; none of the announced duties have been implemented; Chinese officials had said talks were impossible under current circumstances.
Chinese Embassy: unilateral Section 301 violates WTO principles; China will use WTO dispute settlement and take corresponding measures of equal scale and strength.
China industrial production index still ~107 (same period previous year=100) as of 2018-04-01; growth intact.
China reserves excluding gold ~$3.14 trillion in April 2018, essentially stable over the window.
CNY strengthened to 6.2655 per USD on 2018-04-11 from ~6.59 in mid-October 2017; no FX-stress signal yet.
VIX at 20.24 on 2018-04-11, roughly double autumn 2017 levels, with spikes around the 22 March memorandum and early-April list exchange.
